messages:
Carlos (CTO): Quick follow-up from today's roadmap all-hands — thanks for the great questions. I want to collect the remaining runtime clarifications here so leadership can answer them during the live Q&A in 20m. High-level bullets: p99 SLA, kernel rollout ordering (quantized & float), default caching policy differences for hosted vs dedicated. Drop short questions.
Sam (Eng Lead): Short answers so far: p99 target is being tightened (see below) but we need to be explicit about measurement window and synthetic vs real traffic.
Priya (PM): People asked if we can promise the new p99 across all tiers or only Dedicated — clarification pls.
Sam (Eng Lead): The plan: Hosted API will have tiered SLOs. Targeting p99=200ms for small-gen (<=1k tokens) on hosted best-effort, but Dedicated customers can opt into p99=120ms SLAs with reserved pools and tighter autoscaling. Numbers are for 1-2k sequence typical workloads; longer contexts change the SLO.
Marta (SRE): Important add: p99 measurement uses latency.ingress_to_response with a 60s rolling window; we only count successful responses (2xx). We also emit latency.p99_per_model and latency.p99_per_route for dashboards.
Jing (Runtime): Quick kernel question: when we roll an optimized int8 kernel, what's the preferred order — by model family, by region, or by customer-matched traffic?
Theo (Kernel): Prioritization: 1) model family (big wins first, e.g., Llama2 variants), 2) high-impact routes (embedding heavy customers), 3) region parity. We want to maximize global unit-cost reduction while limiting perf regressions. Canary rollout windows default to 2h with 5% traffic, then 25%, then 100% if no regressions.
Priya (PM): Any hardbacks for customers on dedicated if kernel perf regresses?
Sam (Eng Lead): For Dedicated we pin kernel versions per pool by default during major kernel upgrades. We can enable auto-roll for customers who opt in. We also provide automatic fallback rules to previous kernels per-pool if latency.delta > 15% at p95 over the canary window.
Jing (Runtime): Caching config: what's the default TTL and when do we use prefix vs full-key KV cache? Example snippet would help.
Marta (SRE): Defaults: hosted API has cache TTL=30s for generative prefix caching by default, dedicated customers get TTL=60s with a knob for sticky workloads. Prefix caching is used for assistant-style chat where we cache KV for earlier tokens; full-key caching for deterministic reranking/embedding responses.
Jing (Runtime): Example config: ```
cache:
  mode: prefix
  ttl_seconds: 30
  max_entries: 50000
```
Theo (Kernel): Side note — kernel changes that touch KV serialization require an explicit migration window. We'll announce migrations 72h before and run a small validation cohort.
Carlos (CTO): Action items: Sam to post the SLO measurement doc and concrete numbers to docs channel; Priya to update customer comms template for Dedicated pinning; Theo to publish kernel rollout playbook with canary thresholds.
Sam (Eng Lead): I'll drop links in #docs-runtime in 30m.
Deploy Bot: canary-deploy/kv-cache-v2 started for us-west-2 (canary 5%) — monitoring: https://internal.monitor/1887654321
Marta (SRE): I'll watch latency.p99 and kv_cache_hit_ratio, will flag if p99 increases >10% during canary.
Priya (PM): If folks have followups, toss them here or we can take in the live session. Thanks! :rocket:
